messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: sustained 5xx spike on /v1/generate (prod-us-east-1). Metric: runtime.error.rate 12% -> 1xx baseline. Suspected: kv-cache reuse anomalies detected by healthcheck. Paging eli.
eli (oncall): taking this. quick snapshot?
sara (eng-runtime): seeing a cluster-wide jump in sequence mismatch errors in logs: `kv_seq_mismatch` and `kv_stale_value`. It correlates with a config rollout 20m ago that increased continuous_batch.max_tokens from 4096 -> 8192 and enabled aggressive KV reuse flags.
mike (sre): confirmed alerts from infra: a handful of hosts hitting OOMs then heavy GC, followed by 500s. Not all hosts, seems tied to certain model shards.
jen (prod-eng): customer impact: two large customers reported degraded latencies and some incorrect completions (dup tokens). We should assume partial correctness regressions. Not yet a full outage.
eli (oncall): immediate mitigation plan? can we flip the KV reuse flag or roll back batch config?
sara (eng-runtime): two options: 1) disable kv_reuse at runtime (fast feature flag) 2) rollback batching config to previous safe values. Disabling kv_reuse is lower blast radius and can be toggled per-region.
eli (oncall): do it. mike, can you run the flag toggle and watch for error decrease? I'll coordinate with sara for quick checks.
mike (sre): doing `redwood-ops toggle-feature --name kv_reuse --env prod --region us-east-1 --state off` now
ops-bot: command accepted: toggle requested by mike. Rolling out to 12 hosts in us-east-1.
(2m later)
mike (sre): rollout at 40%. error rate dropping on hosts where flag off. overall 5xx down from 12% -> 6%.
sara (eng-runtime): logs show `kv_seq_mismatch` events dropping almost entirely for flag-off hosts. Nice. Still some residual 500s on older hosts where flag hasn't landed.
eli (oncall): keep rolling, start rollback of continuous_batch config if needed. jen, what's customer comms?
jen (prod-eng): opened a pinned incident status page and emailed affected customers w/ initial note: we believe a recent performance tuning caused regressions, working on mitigation. Will update in 30m.
mike (sre): toggle completed across us-east-1. 5xx now 1.8% and dropping. Latency back to baseline in 10s p50.
sara (eng-runtime): OK mitigating. Root cause investigation notes: KV reuse path reused cached KV pages across contexts without validating `seq_offset` after a paged eviction. When batch sizes increased, eviction frequency + reuse race produced stale values returned to other requests -> wrong completions.
eli (oncall): timeline please: when was config rolled?
sara (eng-runtime): rollout started 20m before alert; feature flag for `continuous_batch.max_tokens=8192` was pushed to 20% by auto-ops, then to 60% before we saw spikes. The kv_reuse flag had been flipped on by the tuning PR two days ago but was mostly dormant until batch sizes caused overlapping cache lifetimes.
mike (sre): reproduction step summary for postmortem: run high-concurrency mixed length traffic with batch_max_tokens >= 6k and kv_reuse enabled, simulate paging (eviction) by forcing memory pressure. Observe `kv_seq_mismatch` errors and cross-request duplicate tokens.
eli (oncall): action items (short-term):
- sara: add a runtime guard to verify `seq_offset` before reusing KV entries, and a safe-guard to refuse reuse if TTL/epoch mismatch. (ETA 48h)
- eng-runtime: add unit + integration tests for paged evictions + reuse. (ETA 72h)
- infra/sre: create a canary test to apply large batch sizes in staging with eviction simulation. (ETA 1 week)
- product/eng: revert the auto-rollout policy for continuous_batch until we ship the guard. (jen)
- ops: make the kv_reuse feature flag targetable by pool and model. (mike)

sara (eng-runtime): quick hotfix proposal: add a sequence check at reuse site and fail closed (fallback to recompute) on mismatch. I'll push a small change to hotfix branch and propose a canary deploy to 5 hosts.
eli (oncall): go for canary. keep toggle in case of regressions.

sara (eng-runtime): pushing hotfix now. Here's the patch snippet:
```
// quick guard
if (cached.kv_seq != request.expected_seq) {
  // don't reuse cached kv, regenerate
  metrics.increment("kv.reuse_mismatch")
  goto regen_kv;
}
```

mike (sre): canary deployed to 5 hosts in us-east-1-canary. monitoring.
(5m later)
mike (sre): canary looks good. no 5xx, latency stable, `kv.reuse_mismatch` metric firing ~30x on canary (expected), but no downstream errors.
eli (oncall): schedule progressive rollout of patch and then re-enable kv_reuse only after additional checks.

jen (prod-eng): customer update: "We have identified the cause as a caching regression introduced by a recent batch tuning. A mitigation has been applied and we are verifying recovery; we will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix." :white_check_mark:

eve (note): add to postmortem: failure mode = stale kv reuse due to missing seq validation after paged eviction; contributing factor = aggressive batch size rollout and auto-rollout policy.

sara (eng-runtime): notes for RCA: the reuse logic assumed idempotence of KV entries, but paged storage allowed values to be evicted and reallocated with same slot id; without explicit epoch/seq verification reuse is unsafe.

eli (oncall): closing the live incident: mitigated by disabling kv_reuse and deploying seq-guard hotfix. Remaining work is in the action items. Thanks all for fast ops.

jen (prod-eng): filing follow-up Jira: RED-INC-4389 - "KV cache reuse: seq validation + rollout policy hardening". Assign: eng-runtime + infra.

mike (sre): postmortem meeting scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PT. I'll attach logs and canary graphs.

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident closed at 1718004300.
